name: Floor Descent
description:
The stack of floors and the seed that makes them reproducible. Each descent increments depth and derives the floor's seed from the run seed plus depth — never a fresh random roll, because a floor that changes when you revisit it breaks both speedruns and save audits. The generator lineage matters here: the consuming app's dd-dungeon-generator.ts family already proves this contract in TypeScript outside this repository, and this descriptor is the library-native contract those generators would adapt to, not a port of them. This component owns depth, seeds, and the transition between floors. It owns nothing about room contents — world.room_template stamps the rooms, and whatever lives in them arrives via world.mob_patrol or combat.boss_encounter_script.

SECRET DOORS ARE THE FLOOR'S TO KEEP. Some corridors are hidden: not walkable, not drawn, a wall where their doorway meets the room, until the player searches beside one and the roll succeeds. That is Rogue's mechanic and it lives here because a secret door is a walkability change, and this component is the only thing that says where the floor is -- a second component opening walls would be a second answer to whether a tile can be stood on. A hidden corridor is always an EXTRA route: every room is reachable without it, so a player who never searches is never stranded, and a secret is a shortcut or an alcove rather than the way down. It owns the search roll and the reveal; it does not own the fanfare or the reward -- world.hidden_alcove announces a found space and the listeners decide what it means.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: runSeed
inputs.description: The seed the whole run derives from. Required because a descent with no seed is a different dungeon every load, which is a roguelike decision, not a default.

inputs.name: maxDepth
inputs.description: Floors before the bottom, where the boss or the win condition lives. A depth budget is a session-length budget.

inputs.name: floorSizeByDepth
inputs.description: Room counts and dimensions as a function of depth, as data. Early floors small for pace, deep floors large for stakes. Keyed by depth ('3'), with '*' as the answer for any depth not named; a value is a room count or {rooms, boss?}. `boss: true` lays a boss arena on that floor whatever the cadence says — the default is one every third floor — for a level that wants its fight at the bottom of the first floor.

inputs.name: allowAscent
inputs.description: Whether stairs go back up. Ascent enables retreat-and-return runs; disabling it makes every descent a point of no return.

inputs.name: secretDoors
inputs.description: Hidden corridors per floor, each between two rooms not otherwise adjacent. Zero turns the mechanic off. A floor with fewer than three rooms lays none, because there is no pair left that is not already connected.

inputs.name: searchDifficulty
inputs.description: The d20 target a search beside a hidden doorway must meet. Rogue rolls about one in five per tile per search; 13 is roughly two in five, which makes a second search worth pressing and a fifth not. Zero always finds, forty never does -- both useful for checks and for a genre that wants secrets to be free or fabled.

outputs.name: currentDepth
outputs.description: How far down the party currently is.

outputs.name: currentFloorSeed
outputs.description: The derived seed of the active floor, exposed for regen and debugging.

outputs.name: revision
outputs.description: Increments whenever the floor's walkability changes without the floor itself changing -- a secret door opening. Readers that cache the floor (the pathfinder) key on depth, seed AND this, or they keep routing around a door that is now open.

outputs.name: secretDoors
outputs.description: total and found for the current floor, and the doorway tiles, so a HUD can say '1 secret unfound' without being told where.
